pointers.principle: Rules 1 to 9: input to output, no cog, three attempts, one store, code does mechanical jobs, the verdict the agent cannot edit, herdr is the owner's window, build mode, ships dark

shared-needs.text: Declared, not linked: the shared author writes these volumes and anchors; check.sh matches each need against shared/ when it lands. Nothing below points at a file that does not exist in this pull request.
shared-needs.need: 100 exists or in progress: seat.bundle, workspace, seat.heartbeat, pr.opened, ticket-set.draft; acts: the next node on the edge

412 precondition refused: seat.bundle.refused, workspace.refused (claim_overlap, aggregate, ticket_in_flight, head_moved), seat.result preflight (bundle_mismatch, workspace_mismatch, lease_expired); acts: N-11, or N-03 for claim_overlap without an attempt
429 no capacity: workspace.refused no_slot; acts: N-07 on a later tick, never a waiting loop
500 failed after 3 or a defect: seat.bundle.failed, workspace.failed, phase.failed, validator.failed, launcher.defect; acts: N-11, or N-06 health then N-28 for a defect
file_claims: ticket, pattern, prefix, run_id, at; unique index on prefix for in-flight tickets; released by N-45 on merge, dead or cancel
slots: rows 1..workspace_slots with holder run_id, expires_at; compare-and-swap from null to holder; reclaimed by expiry plus seat.result
no file is ever touched by two open pull requests: declared at cut (N-18), checked at readiness (N-03), checked and recorded at start (N-14), enforced by the fence (N-13) and the diff check (N-16)
every state path lives under $COQ_STATE or $COQ_CACHE, never in the repository, with a registered cleanup script (owner C35)

section.title: Purpose
section.text: N-14 gives a run a place to work: a git worktree cut from origin/main (or from the ticket's existing branch on a later attempt, or detached at a pull request head for a reviewer) in a numbered slot under the cache root, with the ticket's file claims checked and recorded in the store before the seat starts.

It replaces three things that broke: branches cut from whatever the checkout held (memory work-order-start-branches-from-checkout-head: six branches cut from the records branch on 2026-10-11), a start path that dirtied the main checkout and refused 132 seats a day because status was a file on a branch (rebuild/investigation/01-ROOT-CAUSES.md#3-root-causes RC3), and a slot pool whose lease nothing enforced (a 30 hour lease against a 4 hour TTL, rebuild/investigation/L02-state-stores.md section 5 item 7). The main checkout at ~/projects/coq-jev-herdr-plugin is never touched by this node or any other.

The file claim is the mechanical form of the owner's rule that no file is ever touched by two open pull requests (AGENTS.md#law-no-file-is-ever-touched-by-two-open-prs; memory one-file-one-in-flight-ticket): declared at cut (N-18), checked at readiness (N-03), and checked again and recorded here, at the last moment before a seat can write.

section.title: Input record: dispatch
section.text: Kind dispatch, code 100, from N-07; schema ../N-13/record.schema.json#/$defs/dispatch. Fields this node reads: id (becomes run_id), ticket, role, phase, attempt, repo, repo_sha, lease, target.pr and target.head_sha for a reviewer. The validator (N-18) calls the same Provision function with role validator and no ticket to get a detached read-only workspace at origin/main; that call is in-process, not a dispatch, and is recorded as a workspace record with role validator.

section.title: Output record: workspace or workspace.refused
section.text: Kind workspace, code 100, idempotency_key = dispatch.id. Fields: run_id, ticket, role, path ($COQ_CACHE/ws/<slot>/), slot (integer), branch (wo/<ticket-id> for a worker; none for a reviewer, spec-author or validator), base_sha (the commit the worktree was created at), base_ref (origin/main, origin/wo/<ticket>, or refs/pull/<n>/head), mode (write or read-only), claims (the declared file patterns recorded in the store for this ticket, with the claim row id), mirror_sha (origin/main of the mirror at provision time).

Kind workspace.refused, code 412 for an overlap (reason claim_overlap, with the overlapping patterns and the holding ticket id) or 429 for no free slot (reason no_slot, with the pool size and the holders). Kind workspace.failed, code 500 for a git or io failure after 3 attempts (reason fetch_failed, worktree_failed, io).
Schema: record.schema.json#/$defs/workspace, workspace.refused, workspace.failed.

section.title: Mechanism: mirror, worktree, claims, slot
section.text: Package scheduler/internal/workspace in the small Go cut. One function Provision(ctx, dispatch) (workspace, error). Git is run as a child process (git binary, no library) with a timeout per call; every call's argv, exit and stderr tail go to the run's provision.log.
section.mermaid: flowchart TD D[dispatch record, no workspace yet for run_id] --> C{claims: insert file_claims rows for the ticket in one transaction} C -- unique index conflict --> R412[workspace.refused 412 claim_overlap] C -- ok or already held by this ticket --> S{slot: CAS a free row in slots to run_id} S -- none free --> R429[workspace.refused 429 no_slot, claims kept] S -- slot n --> F[fetch in the bare mirror under a flock, timeout 60 s] F --> W[git worktree add --detach ws/n base_ref, then git switch -c or -C branch for a worker] W --> V[verify: git -C ws/n rev-parse HEAD equals base_sha; status clean] V --> P[put workspace 100, idempotency_key = dispatch.id] F -- 3 failures --> R500[workspace.failed 500, slot released, claims kept] W -- 3 failures --> R500
section.step: Claims. Read the ticket record's files (declared at cut by N-18). In one store transaction insert one row per pattern into file_claims (ticket, pattern, prefix, run_id, at). The table has a unique index on prefix for rows whose ticket is in flight (status started, pr open, or awaiting review), where prefix is the literal prefix of the glob before its first wildcard, with a trailing slash meaning the subtree; two patterns overlap when either matches the other's literal prefix (factory/bin/claims.sh header rule). A conflict with another ticket's row is workspace.refused 412 with the holder named; a conflict with this ticket's own rows (attempt n+1) is fine, the rows are reused. A reviewer or validator workspace claims nothing. Aggregates (CHANGELOG.md, INDEX.md, CONTEXT_STATE.md) cannot be claimed: the insert refuses them with 412 reason aggregate.

Slot. The slots table holds rows 1..N where N is scheduler/config/seats.json workspace_slots (default 12). Compare-and-swap one row from holder null to holder run_id with expires_at = dispatch.deadline_at plus 600 s. None free is 429 no_slot; N-07 is level-triggered and will dispatch again when a slot frees, so no one waits in a loop. An expired holder whose run has a seat.result is reclaimed in the same pass (section many-agents).

Mirror. One bare mirror per repository at $COQ_CACHE/git/<slug>.git. Under flock on mirror.lock (wait 30 s), run git fetch --prune origin with a 60 s timeout; the fetch refspecs include +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/* and +refs/pull/*/head:refs/pull/*/head so a reviewer's head is local. Record mirror_sha = origin/main after the fetch.

Worktree. Remove any leftover at ws/<slot> (git worktree remove --force, then rm -rf, then git worktree prune in the mirror). Then git --git-dir mirror worktree add --detach ws/<slot> base_ref where base_ref is: for a worker on attempt 1, origin/main; for a worker on attempt n+1 whose branch exists on origin, origin/wo/<ticket>; for a reviewer, refs/pull/<pr>/head and it must resolve to target.head_sha or the result is 412 head_moved; for a spec-author or validator, origin/main. For a worker, git switch -C wo/<ticket> so the branch is local and tracks origin/wo/<ticket> when it exists. The mirror's push URL is origin; the worktree pushes through the mirror's remote config.

Verify and record. rev-parse HEAD equals base_sha; git status --porcelain is empty; the worktree contains no .claude/settings.local.json (the bundle is outside the tree). Write provision.json beside the worktree (outside it, at $COQ_CACHE/ws/<slot>.json) and put the workspace record with idempotency_key dispatch.id.
section.text: Mode. A worker workspace is write; a reviewer, spec-author or validator workspace is read-only: the settings deny Write and Edit (N-13) and the directory is created with the files read-only for the seat's user is not attempted (same user); the proof is the permission denial in the result, not a filesystem bit.

Branch names. wo/<ticket-id>, one branch per ticket for all its attempts, never a slug (slugs made the old queue search for feat/<slug> by file name, line/bin/seat-queue.sh). Rebuild tickets are plain branches off main with plain pull requests (memory build-mode-rule).

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.text: The seat controller goroutine (N-06 unit, N-07 tick) lists dispatch records with no workspace, workspace.refused or seat.result for the run_id and calls Provision for each, in parallel with the render of N-13; both are children of the same dispatch. A reviewer dispatch arrives only after gate.verdict green (N-08 re-entry), so the head sha it names is the one the gate passed. Nothing in this node is started by a prompt, a pane, a Makefile target typed by hand, or a person.

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.what: store transaction for claims and slot

wait.fallback: workspace.failed 500 mirror_locked; the holder's pid is written in the lock file for the runbook
workspace.failed 500 fetch_failed; the slot is released; the claims stay (the ticket still owns its files)

wait.what: git worktree add, switch, rev-parse, status
wait.fallback: workspace.failed 500 worktree_failed; the slot directory is removed and the slot released
workspace.refused 429 immediately; the next tick tries again; a dispatch older than its deadline with no workspace is a failure record to N-11

section.text: Bound per dispatch: about 7 minutes in the worst case of three slow fetches; no wait depends on a person or an agent.

section.title: Retries up to 3, then recover and report
section.text: Git steps retry 3 times with the backoff above. After the third failure the node writes workspace.failed 500 with the step, reason and stderr tail, releases the slot, keeps the claims, and stops. N-11 counts the attempt; a dead record after 3 attempts becomes one owner card (N-28). On service restart the controller re-lists dispatches without a workspace; a slot row whose holder has no live run and no seat.result older than its expires_at is reclaimed with its directory removed. A claims row whose ticket reached merged, dead or cancelled is released by N-45 on the merge or dead record, never by this node.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.text: Readers: twenty seats can be provisioned in one tick; the controller runs Provision in a pool of seats.json provision_workers (default 4), bounded by the mirror lock on the fetch only; worktree creation runs in parallel because each slot is its own directory.

Collision 1, two tickets declare overlapping files: the unique index on file_claims.prefix for in-flight tickets makes the second insert fail inside its transaction; it is refused 412 and the ticket returns to waiting in N-03. Both cannot hold the same prefix, by the database, not by a script reading gh pr list (factory/bin/claims.sh read GitHub and a worktree list, which a seat on another machine made invisible; the store is the one authority, D04 and D10).

Collision 2, two passes provision the same dispatch: the slot CAS admits one holder per slot, the workspace put is idempotent by dispatch.id, and the loser's worktree is removed by the cleanup of unrecorded slots in the next pass.

Collision 3, the same ticket is dispatched twice with different run ids (a lease fencing failure upstream): the claims rows carry run_id; the second insert for the same ticket updates run_id only if the first run has a seat.result; otherwise it is refused 412 reason ticket_in_flight and reported as a defect record, because N-02 should have prevented it.
Collision 4, two fetches at once: the flock serializes them; a fetch that finds the mirror already fresh (origin/main unchanged within 10 s) is skipped.

Collision 5, a reviewer workspace while the worker's branch moves: the reviewer is detached at the head sha the gate passed; a new push makes a new head sha, a new gate.verdict and a new reviewer dispatch; the old review result is discarded by N-19 as head_moved.

Collision 6, cleanup (N-45) and a live run on one slot: cleanup removes only a slot whose run has a seat.result and whose branch is merged or whose ticket is dead; a slot with a live holder is never touched, by a CAS on the slot row before any rm.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.code: Provisioned. Acts: N-15 when the seat.bundle also exists.

claim_overlap, aggregate, ticket_in_flight, head_moved. Acts: N-11 as a failure record; claim_overlap returns the ticket to N-03 waiting without counting an attempt (the ticket did nothing wrong; it is a scheduling order), the others count.
no_slot. Acts: N-07 retries on a later tick; never a seat waiting in a loop; a dispatch past its deadline with no workspace is a failure record.
fetch_failed, worktree_failed, mirror_locked, store_unreachable, io. Acts: N-11.

section.title: State paths and the cleanup script for each

path.retention: kept; git gc --prune weekly; worktree prune every run

section.path: Dry run by default; --apply runs gc and prune; never deletes the mirror while any slot row has a holder.

path.writes: the worktree and its provision record
path.retention: removed on merge, dead or cancel (N-45 trigger), or 24 h after the run's seat.result when no record triggered

section.path: Dry run lists slot, holder, run, branch, dirty state; --apply removes only slots whose CAS from holder to null succeeds; a dirty worktree with unpushed commits is listed as kept and reported as a record (never deleted silently, specs/SPEC-04-herdr-seat-lifecycle.xml#s-cleanup rule carried forward).

path.writes: git argv, exit codes, stderr tails

section.text: $COQ_CACHE resolves through bin/state-root.sh (default ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/coq/coq-jev-herdr-plugin). Both scripts are registered in N-45's scheduler/config/cleanup.json. The repository holds the scripts; nothing under $COQ_CACHE or $COQ_STATE is ever committed (C35; AGENTS.md#law-runtime-data-never-lives-in-git).

section.title: Permissions
section.text: The Go service: read and write under $COQ_CACHE/ws and $COQ_CACHE/git; run git; network to origin (fetch only; pushes happen in N-16's close-out through the same mirror remote with the owner's git credential helper on the host); gRPC to the store. No GitHub API token is needed to provision; the reviewer head is fetched by refspec.

A seat: receives the workspace path as its cwd and COQ_WORKTREE; may write only inside allow_paths of its bundle; never runs git worktree, git switch, treehouse or rm -rf of the slot (denied commands in N-13). A seat that needs another workspace cannot get one: it reports blocked.

section.title: Checklist with proof

item.proof: go test ./internal/workspace -run TestClaimOverlapRefused: two tickets declaring herdr/bin/* and herdr/bin/seat.sh; the second Provision returns workspace.refused 412 naming the first ticket; the store shows one claims row set

section.item: Overlap is refused by the store's unique index.

item.proof: go test TestConcurrentProvisionOneSlot: 20 concurrent Provision calls against a pool of 12 yield 12 workspace records and 8 refused 429, with 12 distinct slots

section.item: Slots are handed out by compare-and-swap.

item.proof: go test TestBaseRefByPhase: attempt 1 worker is at origin/main; attempt 2 with the branch on origin is at origin/wo/WO-x; reviewer is at refs/pull/N/head and equals target.head_sha; a moved head returns 412 head_moved

section.item: Base ref follows the phase and attempt.

item.proof: probe: git -C ~/projects/coq-jev-herdr-plugin status --porcelain before and after 50 provisions is byte-identical

section.item: The main checkout is never touched.

item.proof: probe: a fetch with origin unreachable (bogus URL) returns workspace.failed 500 fetch_failed after 3 attempts within 7 minutes and the slot row is null again

section.item: Fetch failure is bounded and releases the slot.

item.proof: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-workspaces.sh --dry-run lists a merged slot as removable and a dirty slot as kept; --apply removes only the first
scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-git-mirror.sh --dry-run prints the gc and prune it would run; --apply exits 0 and the mirror still serves a fetch
make lint: scheduler/config/seats.json validates against seats.schema.json with workspace_slots, provision_workers present

section.item: Pool size is config, not a role field.

section.title: Monitoring
section.text: Counters: workspaces_provisioned, workspaces_refused_overlap, workspaces_refused_slot, workspaces_failed, slots_in_use, provision_seconds histogram, mirror_fetch_seconds. The Machine screen (N-39) for this node shows slots in use over the pool as a belt occupancy. A 429 streak longer than seats.json slot_starvation_seconds (default 900) is an alert on N-41 because capacity, not seats, is the defect (D17 option B).

section.title: Runbook
section.text: See slots: scheduler status (gRPC Status) lists slots with holder, run, ticket, since. See a workspace: cat $COQ_CACHE/ws/<slot>.json; git -C $COQ_CACHE/ws/<slot> status.
Mirror stuck under its lock: the lock file names the pid; if the pid is gone, the next Provision pass removes the stale lock (flock releases on process death anyway); never delete the mirror by hand.

Cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-workspaces.sh [--apply] [--slot N]; scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-git-mirror.sh [--apply]. Both run from N-45's timer; a hand run is the owner's break glass and is recorded by the script as a cleanup.run with by owner.
A dirty slot that cleanup keeps: the record names the branch and the unpushed commits; the disposition is a card (N-28) with options land as a pull request or discard; never discarded by the script.

section.title: DAG edges in and out

edge.record: workspace.refused 412 claim_overlap returns the ticket to waiting without an attempt

section.text: N-18 calls Provision in process for its verify workspace; that is not a drawn edge because it is a library call inside the same service, recorded as a workspace record with role validator.
